recommendation: Fund billing_support first, led by free-tier feature restrictions (ISS-billing-free_tier_restrictions). Treat the generic 'other' issue as not fundable. Fund ads frequency as a second item only if scope permits, and keep playback stops/pauses as the first alternative if leadership prioritizes severity over volume.
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation

**Priority area: billing_support.** Fund first: (1) **free-tier restrictions** (ISS-billing-free_tier_restrictions), the highest-ranked specific issue; (2) **ads frequency and length** (ISS-usability-ads_frequency), which is closely tied to the free/premium experience; (3) as a reliability companion, **music stops/pauses/skips** (ISS-playback-stops_pauses_skips). The rank 1 issue, ISS-other-general_negative (86,666 complaints [C001], priority score 173,771 [C004]), is generic criticism with no specific product problem. We report it but it is not a fundable priority.

## Why

Free-tier restrictions have 47,460 complaints [C005], a severity sum of 138,070 [C006], and mean severity 2.909187 [C007]. At topic-group level, billing_support has 58,239 complaints [T007], a severity sum of 167,534 [T008], 4,853 severity 4+ records [T010], and 12,786 cancellation-language records [T011], the most of any group. It is 19.8% of all complaints [T012].

The trend is sharp. Billing_support rose from 6,165 complaints (3.51%) in the early window to 39,530 (13.12%) in the late window, based on full months only. Other also rose, from 5,397 to 71,188, and its late-window share is the largest, but it is non-specific.

Customers say:
- "The new updates are terrible I can't even select the songs I want." [R:1fdec127-9ebc-4cc1-87ab-f23c8e8c0624]
- "...limit the skips of songs and to remove the ability to go back..." [R:40e7479a-4547-4936-ba92-c2711aa7037e]
- "Now suddenly... the ads have started playing after 2 songs and I find it annoying." [R:f7ccd28b-4083-4d9b-9833-d6899fe9244e]

Ads frequency has 36,113 complaints [C009] and a priority score of 77,831 [C012].

## Alternatives considered

- **Usability:** 66,061 complaints [T013], the largest specific group by volume, but mean severity is lower at 2.390730 [T015] and only 1,491 severity 4+ records [T016]. Its volume is mainly ads, which we already include, plus navigation and queue issues (12,110 [C029] and 11,226 [C025] complaints).
- **Playback:** 38,451 complaints [T019] at mean severity 3.289719 [T021], with 15,390 severity 4+ records [T022]. Stops/pauses/skips has 14,242 complaints [C013] and a score of 47,394 [C016]. It ranks lower on volume and score and its late share fell, from 13,284 (7.56%) to 12,316 (4.09%). It would rise if severity is weighted over breadth, or if the quarter targets driving and offline use.
- **Access:** only 10,311 complaints [T031], but the highest mean severity at 3.868684 [T033] and 8,989 severity 4+ records [T034]. Login failure has 8,528 complaints [C021]. It is a good targeted fix, but its reach is small. Quotes: "For some inexplicable reason, I was logged out of my account." [R:77f29c25-d52e-4380-997c-77022d5ddcf1]

## Limitations

- Reviews are self-selected and public, so they are not representative of all users.
- There is no revenue, plan, or churn data. Cancellation language is stated intent, not observed churn.
- Of 660,622 source rows, 660,503 were completed and 119 quarantined. 176,420 were completed via exact text reuse, and 104,769 were flagged needs-review.
- A verifier sample of 200 showed topic agreement of 0.75 and severity MAE of 0.26. The 50-case golden set showed topic agreement of 0.62 and severity MAE of 0.38, so label noise is material, particularly in topic assignment.
- The baseline score weights complaint count by severity, which favors high-volume, moderate-severity issues. Rankings may shift under other weightings.
- Issues were assigned one per review, and the share of 'other' is large (31.1% [T006]).
